correctness.rationale: Full-row/full-column coverage plus nonisolation characterize total domination. Minimality follows from the exact private-neighbor condition; a two-way classification by covered rows, selected row degrees and possible double columns yields disjoint labeled counts. Boundary collisions n=3 and n=6 are explicitly included. Independent direct open-neighborhood subset enumeration checks all 2,396,667 nonempty subsets across n=3..7; finite checks corroborate the proof but do not establish the infinite statement.

evidence: Brešar et al., arXiv:2310.07432, bound upper total domination and zero forcing in general graphs; their general inequality is weaker and does not determine numbers of minimal total dominating sets.
Golovach et al., DOI:10.1016/j.dam.2014.12.010, provide algorithmic minimal-dominating-set enumeration on chordal bipartite graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General bounds, enumeration algorithms and other domination variants do not imply coefficientwise counts. The rook graph contains triangles and is not in the chordal-bipartite graph class. No inspected general structural theorem specializes to the full claimed distribution.

originality.rationale: The complete labeled cardinality polynomial of inclusion-minimal total dominating sets in K_3 Cartesian K_n and its unbounded spectrum gaps were not implied by the inspected total-edge-domination, well-totally-dominated, upper-total-domination, or generic minimal-domination-enumeration publications. Equivalent graph-operation terminology and stronger possible general statements were assessed. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of publication priority.

value.rationale: Rook graphs are natural line graphs of complete bipartite graphs. The first nontrivial fixed-width family is structurally tractable yet displays unexpected extreme gaps in attainable cardinalities of inclusion-minimal total dominating sets, up to unbounded length; the theorem supplies every coefficient and exact exceptions, not just a routine scalar parameter. This is useful for studying minimal total edge domination, extremal minimal-set spectra, and domination enumeration.
